mnemonic: 忄 a heart with 布 a cloth thrown over it, hiding. Doesn't matter how small the dog is or whose it is. You're already behind someone: こわい.
notes: Does both jobs: the person who is afraid, and the thing that is frightening.
sentence_meaning: I'm scared of dogs.

sentence: 韓国に5年いました。
mnemonic: One harvest carried in, then another, and you count them off. Five of them in Korea before you looked up: 5年, ごねん.
notes: Same kanji as 年 とし. ねん is the one that sits behind a number and counts.
sentence_meaning: I was in South Korea for five years.

notes: Same kanji as 年 ねん, which only counts. とし is the year as a thing in itself, the reading you already met in 毎年 まいとし.
sentence_meaning: A new year has started.
sentence: 新しい年が始まりました。
mnemonic: The same harvest as ねん, except nobody is counting it. A whole new one has just started and it's still completely empty: とし.

sentence: テストでいい点を取った。
mnemonic: 耳 an ear with 又 a hand closed round it. Old soldiers took ears off the field to prove the count. You took a good mark off that test: とる.
sentence_meaning: I got a good grade on the test.

mnemonic: 全 a king under one roof, and everything under that roof with him. You told him the lot, nothing held back at all: すべて.
sentence: 彼に全てのことを伝えた。
sentence_meaning: I told him everything.
notes: 全部 ぜんぶ is the everyday spoken one; 全て leans a little more written.

sentence: 彼女は病気の犬を助けた。
mnemonic: 力 power stuck on the right-hand side. An extra shoulder put under the load. The dog was ill in a ditch and she carried it home: たすける.
notes: Stronger than English 'help'. It stretches all the way to rescuing and saving a life.
sentence_meaning: She helped a sick dog.
It will be difficult to depart in these conditions.
sentence: この状況では出発は難しいです。
mnemonic: 状 the shape a thing has taken, with 犬 a dog in it, and 況 water running past. Look at the state of it. Nobody is setting off in this: じょうきょう.

sentence_meaning: I confirmed my reservation one more time.
notes: 確認する is one of the most common words in Japanese office life. Checking a thing before it goes wrong.
mnemonic: 確 a 石 stone, solid enough to be sure of, and 認 words you finally accept. You check the booking one more time anyway: かくにん.
sentence: もう一度、予約を確認した。

sentence_meaning: The light is off, so Tanaka-san must not be in this room.
notes: 消す けす is you turning it off; 消える is it going out. Same split as 出る and 出す.
mnemonic: 氵 water on the left, wearing something away until there's nothing there. The light is off and the room has gone with it: きえる.
sentence: 電気が消えているので、田中さんは部屋にいないでしょう。
彼女の髪はとても長い。
mnemonic: Long hair on an old figure, drawn flowing all the way down the character. Hers goes past where the drawing stops: ながい.
notes: Length in space or in time. The same kanji reads ちょう in 社長 しゃちょう, a company head.
sentence_meaning: Her hair is very long.

mnemonic: 馬 a horse underneath the whole thing, and something has just gone off beside it. A shout in an empty street at two in the morning and you come off the ground: おどろく.
sentence: 夜中に道で大きな声がして、驚きました。
meaning: to be surprised, to be astonished
sentence_meaning: I was surprised by a loud voice on the street in the middle of the night.
Please rotate your arm.
notes: Also means skill. 腕がいい is 'good at it', the way English says a safe pair of hands.
mnemonic: The 月 that means flesh, with a shape for bending sat beside it. The physio wants it all the way round, both directions: うで.
sentence: 腕を回してください。

sentence_meaning: I go to school by bicycle except on rainy days.
notes: Same 以 as 以上 いじょう. 以上 counts from a point upward; 以外 cuts one thing out and keeps the rest.
mnemonic: 以 the marker that fixes a boundary, and 外 everything sat outside it. Every day on the bike, and rain filed on the far side of the line: いがい.
sentence: 私は雨の日以外は自転車で学校に行く。

sentence_meaning: I'm at a loss because I lost my cell phone.
meaning: to be at a loss, to be troubled
sentence: ケータイをなくして困っています。
mnemonic: 木 a tree boxed inside 囗 four walls, with nowhere left to grow. Phone gone, every number in it, and you're standing there doing nothing: こまる.

sentence_meaning: I was away from my parents' house for 4 years.
meaning: to be separated, to be apart
mnemonic: 隹 a small bird on the right, gone off the branch and not coming back to it. Four years away from your parents' house before you saw it again: はなれる.
sentence: 実家を4年間離れていました。

sentence_meaning: She asked if I was willing to travel.
notes: Turns up in a huge number of set phrases: 気をつけて be careful, 気にしないで don't worry about it.
mnemonic: Steam coming off something, the same 気 that sits in 元気. On its own it's whatever you've got rising in you. And she wants to know if any of it is for travelling: き.
sentence: 旅行に行く気があるか彼女に聞かれました。

mnemonic: 聿 a hand gripping a brush, sat straight down on the thing it's marking. A whole letter to him, by hand, and then you had to post it: かく.
sentence: 彼に手紙を書きました。
sentence_meaning: I wrote him a letter.
notes: 描く かく is the same sound for drawing a picture. Writing is 書く.

sentence: この部屋は光がたくさん入って、いいね。
mnemonic: A figure on 儿 legs with brightness coming off the top of its head. Whoever built this room pointed it the right way, the stuff pours in: ひかり.
notes: 光る ひかる is the verb, to shine.
sentence_meaning: It’s nice how much light comes into this room, isn’t it?

mnemonic: 土 the earth up top with legs driving away underneath it. Three kilometres of it, every night, in the dark, without being asked: はしる.
sentence: 彼は毎晩3キロ走っています。
sentence_meaning: Every night he runs three kilometers.

mnemonic: 戈 a halberd stood up on the right-hand side, and somebody still holding it. 最後 the very last moment, and he had not put it down: たたかう.
sentence: 彼は最後まで戦ったよ。
sentence_meaning: He fought to the very end.
Let's use the left-over portion next time.
notes: Same word as the kana あまり 'not very'. With a negative it means there isn't much of something, and this is the something.
mnemonic: A roof with whatever didn't get used stacked underneath it. Too much fabric, too much batter, and none of it thrown away: あまり.
sentence: 余りは次回使いましょう。

mnemonic: 全 the whole thing and 部 every section of it accounted for. The lunchbox goes back empty, not most of it, all of it: ぜんぶ.
sentence: お弁当を全部食べました。
sentence_meaning: I ate all that was in the lunchbox.
notes: The everyday spoken one. 全て すべて is the same idea, a shade more written.

sentence_meaning: At that instant, the cat ran out.
notes: 間 reads かん here, the same as in 時間 じかん.
mnemonic: 目 an eye on the left, open exactly as long as a blink, and 間 the gap it makes. That's how much warning you got before the cat went: しゅんかん.
sentence: その瞬間、猫が跳び出しました。

mnemonic: 説 words worked at until they come loose, and 明 the sun and moon making it bright. Neither of those has happened to this grammar page: せつめい.
sentence: この文法の説明は良く分かりません。
sentence_meaning: I don't really understand the explanation of this grammar.

notes: 決まる きまる is it being decided; 決める is somebody deciding it.
sentence_meaning: Let's decide the time of the meeting.
sentence: 会議の時間を決めましょう。
mnemonic: 氵 water on the left, cut a channel and it only runs one way after that. Pick the time for the meeting and everyone else's day pours into it: きめる.

sentence: そのパーティーに女性は何人来ますか。
mnemonic: 女 a woman with 性 a 忄 heart and 生 a life beside her, the whole person, not just the label. This is the word you use in front of people: じょせい.
notes: The polite one. Bare 女 おんな can sound blunt about a person; 女性 never does.
sentence_meaning: How many women are coming to that party?

mnemonic: 頂 is the very top of a thing, 頁 a head with the crown marked on it. You take the sweets with both hands and your own head goes down: いただく.
sentence: お客様にお菓子を頂いた。
sentence_meaning: A customer gave me some snacks.
notes: The humble version of 受ける and もらう: it lowers you, not them. It's also the いただきます said before eating.

sentence_meaning: The enemy is lurking there.
sentence: あそこに敵がひそんでいる。
mnemonic: 攵 the strike radical stood on the right, waiting. Somebody is behind that wall and they are not on your side: てき.

notes: Same word as 起きる "to get up". Events use it too: a thing rises up and happens.
sentence_meaning: Some burglaries occurred in the neighborhood.
sentence: 近所で盗難事件が起きました。
mnemonic: 走 running with 己 yourself behind it. Something stands up out of nowhere. Three break-ins on your own street, and none of them were there last week: おきる.

sentence: 私は毎朝6時に起きます。
mnemonic: The same standing-up as the one events do, only this time it's you. Six o'clock, every single morning, upright before you've decided to be: おきる.
notes: Same word as 起きる "to occur". Careful with 怒る おこる, to get angry, one vowel apart.
meaning: to get up, to get out of bed
sentence_meaning: I get up at six o'clock every morning.
My bag fell down there.
notes: 落とす おとす is you dropping it; 落ちる is it falling by itself.
mnemonic: 艹 grass and 氵 water up at the top of the character, both on their way down. Your bag goes off the rack and lands somewhere under the seat: おちる.
sentence: 荷物が下に落ちてしまいました。

mnemonic: 口 a knee drawn on top of the foot underneath it. His go on for ever, trousers never fit him off the peg: あし.
sentence: 彼は足が長い。
sentence_meaning: He has long legs.
notes: Covers the whole thing, leg and foot together. Japanese doesn't split them the way English does.

sentence_meaning: Hotel fares are expensive during extended weekends. In addition, it's crowded everywhere.
notes: Piles a second point onto the first. そして just adds the next thing; それで says the first caused the second.
mnemonic: The hotels cost double over the long weekend. それに. And on top of that, every single place is heaving. One complaint stacked straight onto another.
sentence: 連休はホテル代が高いです。それに、どこも人が多いです。

mnemonic: 先 a figure striding out in front on 儿 legs, the same 先 as 先生. You're off now and they can catch up later: さきに.
sentence: では、私たちは先に出発します。
sentence_meaning: We will leave before you then.
notes: お先に失礼します is the standard line for leaving the office before your colleagues.

mnemonic: 魔 a demon crouched under the roof, and 法 water finding the one way down. She's behaving as though somebody set that loose on her: まほう.
sentence: 彼女はまるで魔法にかかったみたいだ。
sentence_meaning: She acts as if she is under a spell.

mnemonic: 扌 a hand reaching right down into somewhere deep and feeling about. Every shop, every week, still no pink jumper: さがす.
sentence: ピンクのセーターをずっと探しています。
sentence_meaning: I've been looking for a pink sweater for a while.

mnemonic: 子 a child with 供 more of them along for the ride. Not one of them on the whole carriage is sitting still: こども.
sentence: 電車で子供が騒いでいた。
sentence_meaning: Kids were making a racket in the train.
notes: Same 子 as 子 こ. 子供 is the ordinary standalone word for a child.

sentence_meaning: He was angry because she lied.
notes: One vowel from 起きる おきる, to get up. Also covers telling someone off, not just being cross.
mnemonic: 奴 a servant sat on top of 心 the heart, and the heart underneath is doing all the work. She lied and he has gone quiet in a way that isn't quiet: おこる.
sentence: 彼女が嘘をついたので、彼は怒った。

sentence_meaning: The baby's smile is cute.
notes: 笑う わらう is the verb. 笑顔 is the face, and it's the word you'd use for a photo.
mnemonic: 笑 bamboo bent double and 顔 a face to put it on. Not the laugh itself, the face doing it. And on a baby it finishes you: えがお.
sentence: 赤ちゃんの笑顔が可愛い。

mnemonic: 先 the one out in front, with 輩 a row of carts strung out behind. They joined a year before you and that never stops counting: せんぱい.
sentence: 先輩からメール来た？
sentence_meaning: Did you get a text from your senior?
notes: 後輩 こうはい is the other end, anyone who joined after you. The pair runs your whole working life.

sentence: 雨の日が２週間も続いています。
mnemonic: 糸 a thread that nobody has cut. Two full weeks of rain, one day joined onto the next, and no end showing: つづく.
notes: 続ける つづける is you keeping something going; 続く is it going on by itself.
sentence_meaning: Rainy days have continued for two weeks.

mnemonic: こ- is the near one again, the same こ as これ. You're holding the book up so somebody can see how much you mean: こんなに.
sentence: こんなに面白い本は初めて読んだ。
sentence_meaning: It's the first time I read such an interesting book.
notes: そんなに is that much, over by them; あんなに is that much, over there.

mnemonic: The same 変 as 変わる, one thing turning into another. But caught halfway, when it isn't either. Something in the wall is making a noise it shouldn't: へん.
sentence: 変な音が聞こえます。
sentence_meaning: I hear a strange sound.
notes: Same kanji as 変わる かわる and 変える かえる, which are the verbs. 変 on its own is the adjective.

mnemonic: 言 speech with 売 selling beside it. The words were written down to be handed on. You take them off the page in Japanese now: よむ.
sentence: 日本語の本を読みます。
sentence_meaning: I read a Japanese language book.

mnemonic: 当 landing squarely on the spot and 然 that being how it is. She was lied to. Of course she's angry. Where else was that going to land: とうぜん.
sentence: 彼女が怒るのも当然だ。
meaning: natural, as a matter of course
sentence_meaning: It's natural that she would be angry.
notes: Shares its 然 with 全然 ぜんぜん.

sentence_meaning: I'd like to know some information about the hotel.
notes: Shares its 情 with 表情 ひょうじょう, where the feeling shows on the outside instead.
mnemonic: 情 what's going on inside a thing, and 報 a hand passing the news of it over. Everything about the hotel that isn't on the front page: じょうほう.
sentence: 私はホテルの情報が知りたいです。

sentence_meaning: I found a new job.
notes: 見る みる is looking, 見える みえる is it being visible, 見つける is the moment you land on it.
mnemonic: 見 an eye on legs and 付 a hand fixing onto what it saw. Months of looking, and then a job. Spotted and taken hold of: みつける.
sentence: 新しい仕事を見つけました。

notes: A written, slightly literary word. In speech you'd say 女の子 おんなのこ.
sentence_meaning: The girl clasped her mother's hand.
sentence: 少女は母親の手を握った。
mnemonic: 少 a small amount of 女 woman, not grown yet. She reaches up and takes her mother's hand without looking: しょうじょ.

notes: Also does duty as 'very' in front of an adjective: 大変おいしい is very tasty. Same 変 as 変 へん.
sentence_meaning: A terrible thing happened.
sentence: 大変なことが起こりました。
mnemonic: 大 big and 変 strange stuck together, a large amount of something going badly wrong. Whatever has happened, it isn't small: たいへん.

notes: Stronger than ちょっと, softer than とても. It carries a small note of surprise.
sentence_meaning: He's pretty good at English.
sentence: 彼はかなり英語が上手です。
mnemonic: More than you were expecting, less than you'd call fluent. He opens his mouth and you quietly adjust upwards: かなり.

sentence: 財布は机の下にあった。
mnemonic: A mark sitting below the line, the exact mirror of 上. Your purse has been under the desk the entire time you've been turning the house over: した.
notes: Same kanji as 下 もと. した is physically underneath. It also reads か and げ in compounds. 地下 ちか is underground.
sentence_meaning: My purse was under the desk.

mnemonic: The same mark below the line as した, except nothing is physically on top of you. You wrote the whole thesis in that professor's shadow: もと.
sentence: 私はその教授の下で論文を書いたの。
sentence_meaning: I wrote my thesis under that professor's supervision.
notes: Same kanji as 下 した. した is under a desk; もと is under someone's authority, a boss, a professor, a rule.

sentence: 自転車で10分ぐらいかかります。
mnemonic: Ten minutes on the bike and you don't get to argue about it. かかる is the meter running: the thing costs whatever it costs.
notes: Same sound as 掛かる かかる 'to hang', but this one is normally written in kana. 時間がかかる, お金がかかる.
sentence_meaning: It takes about 10 minutes by bicycle.

notes: 掛ける かける is you hanging it; 掛かる is it hanging. Same sound as the kana かかる, 'to take time'.
sentence_meaning: A beautiful calendar is hanging, isn't it?
sentence: 綺麗なカレンダーが掛かっていますね。
mnemonic: 扌 a hand at a peg, the same 掛 as 掛ける. But nobody's hand is on it now. The calendar is simply up there, being beautiful at you: かかる.
一 one and 度 a single turn of the wheel. Flower viewing, exactly the one time, years ago, and you still bring it up: いちど.
sentence: 一度、花見をしたことがあります。
sentence_meaning: I went flower viewing once before.
notes: Same 度 as 今度 こんど. もう一度 もういちど is 'one more time'.

sentence_meaning: This old Buddhist temple still maintains its complete form.
mnemonic: 完 everything finished off under 宀 one roof, and 全 the whole of it still there. The temple has not lost a single beam in a thousand years: かんぜん.
sentence: この古い寺院は今でも完全な形を保っているんだ。
後ろを向いて。
mnemonic: The same 後 you already have as あと, but aimed at space instead of time. Not later, behind you. Turn round and look: うしろ.
notes: Same kanji as 後 あと 'after' and the ご in 今後. うしろ is the physical one.
sentence_meaning: Turn around.

sentence: 妹はすぐに泣く。
mnemonic: 氵 water beside 立 somebody standing there. She hasn't moved and she hasn't said anything, and it's already coming down her face: なく.
notes: Tears. 鳴く なく is the identical sound for the noise an animal makes.
sentence_meaning: My little sister cries easily.
The road is in a very bad state here.
notes: Shares its 状 with 状況 じょうきょう. 状態 is the condition a thing is in; 状況 is the situation going on around it.
mnemonic: 状 the shape a thing has taken, with 態 putting 心 a heart under it. Look at the state of this road, potholes the entire way along: じょうたい.
sentence: ここは道の状態がとても悪いです。

notes: 関係ない is one of the most common phrases going: 'nothing to do with me'.
sentence_meaning: He has nothing to do with that incident.
sentence: 彼はその事件に関係がない。
mnemonic: 関 a gate with the bar across it, and 係 a person tied onto a line running through. He isn't anywhere on that line. Nothing connects him to it: かんけい.

sentence: 彼は上司に怒りの目を向けたんだよ。
mnemonic: 向 the window that only faces one way, except now somebody has turned it. He puts both eyes on his boss and leaves them there: むける.
notes: 向かう むかう is heading that way yourself; 向ける is aiming something else.
meaning: to turn toward, to point at
sentence_meaning: He stared with angry eyes at his superior.

notes: Same sound as 置く おく, 'to put'. 奥 is the depths of something. And 奥さん is somebody's wife.
sentence_meaning: The scissors were at the back of the desk.
sentence: はさみは机の奥にあった。
mnemonic: Something shut deep inside the frame with 大 spread across the bottom to keep it in. The scissors were at the very back of the drawer the whole time: おく.

sentence_meaning: These shoes are very light.
notes: Also light in the sense of not serious. 軽い風邪 is a mild cold.
mnemonic: 車 a cart on the left, built light enough for one person to pull. You brace to lift the shoes and nearly put them through the ceiling: かるい.
sentence: この靴はとても軽い。

sentence_meaning: I returned the book to the library.
notes: Careful: 帰る かえる is you going home and 変える かえる is altering something. 返す is giving a thing back.
mnemonic: 辶 the road with 反 something turned over on it. Back the way you came, carrying the thing. The book goes into the library slot: かえす.
sentence: 図書館に本を返した。

sentence_meaning: The sun appeared between the clouds.
sentence: 雲の間から太陽が現れました。
mnemonic: 王 a jewel with 見 an eye brought up to it. The instant a thing becomes visible. The cloud slides off and the sun is simply there: あらわれる.

sentence: 歯が痛いです。
mnemonic: 疒 the sickness radical wrapped the whole way round it. One tooth, and it has taken over that entire side of your head: いたい.
notes: Also what you shout when it happens. 痛い is the Japanese for 'ouch'.
sentence_meaning: My tooth hurts.

sentence: 明日はどうやら雨らしいよ。
mnemonic: Nobody has confirmed a thing. But the forecast, the sky and the way your knee feels all agree. どうやら it's raining tomorrow.
notes: Usually has らしい or ようだ waiting later in the sentence.
sentence_meaning: Seems like it's going to rain tomorrow.

sentence: 電気を点けてください。
mnemonic: 灬 fire down at the bottom, and 点 is one single spot of it. Somebody has to go and put a light to the room: つける.
notes: Same sound as 付ける つける. This one is for anything that lights up, lamps, switches, the telly.
sentence_meaning: Please turn on the light.
I added a freebie.
meaning: to attach, to set, to add
notes: Same sound as 点ける つける, which is for lights. This is attaching anything to anything, and it's the same 付 as 見つける.
mnemonic: 亻 a person and 寸 a hand, pressing one thing onto another. Not the light this time, a freebie slipped into the bag on top of the order: つける.
sentence: おまけを付けました。

sentence_meaning: I doubted my ears for an instant.
notes: 瞬間 しゅんかん is the moment itself; 一瞬 is 'for an instant', and behaves like an adverb.
mnemonic: 一 one 瞬 blink, the same 瞬 that sits in 瞬間. That is precisely how long you spent not believing your own ears: いっしゅん.
sentence: 一瞬自分の耳を疑ったよ。
僕に隠していることは無いですか。
mnemonic: 阝 a hill on the left and something tucked round the back of it. Is there anything behind yours?. Asked in the voice that already knows: かくす.
notes: 隠れる かくれる is you hiding yourself; 隠す is hiding something.
sentence_meaning: Is there anything you're hiding from me?

mnemonic: 準 water levelled off flat, and 備 a person with everything laid out ready beside them. Tomorrow's meeting, the whole of it sorted tonight: じゅんび.
sentence: 明日の会議の準備をした。
sentence_meaning: I prepared for tomorrow's meeting.
It's about time to begin.
notes: Softens whatever comes after it. そろそろ帰ります is the polite way to announce you're going.
mnemonic: Nobody has said anything, but people have started looking at the clock and gathering their coats. そろそろ. Shall we make a start, then?
sentence: そろそろ始めましょうか。

mnemonic: 落ちる falling and 着く landing, bolted together. Everything that was up in the air comes down and stays down. Sit. Now listen: おちつく.
sentence: 私の話を落ち着いて聞いてください。
sentence_meaning: Calm down and listen to me.
meaning: to calm down, to settle in
notes: Built straight out of 落ちる おちる. Also used of settling into a new place, and of a room that feels calm.

sentence_meaning: It was very embarrassing.
notes: Covers embarrassed and shy at once. The feeling, and the thing that causes it.
mnemonic: 耳 an ear sat over 心 the heart, because the ears are the part that gives you away. Both of them scarlet before you'd even finished the sentence: はずかしい.
sentence: とても恥ずかしかった。

mnemonic: 場 a place, the same 場 as 場所, with 合 things fitting together in it. The particular set of circumstances you find yourself in, stuck, in this case: ばあい.
sentence: 分からない場合は私に聞いてください。
sentence_meaning: Please ask me in case you don't understand.

mnemonic: Both hands, and no daylight between your fingers. Whatever it is, it is not going to be the one that slips: しっかり.
sentence: 両手でしっかり持って。
sentence_meaning: Hold it firmly with both hands.
notes: Same word as しっかり "reliable". This one is about grip, the other is about a person.

sentence_meaning: He is reliable even though he is young.
notes: Same word as しっかり "tightly". Said of a person it means solid and dependable.
mnemonic: The same grip as holding something in both hands, turned on a person instead. He's twenty-three and nothing has ever been dropped: しっかり.
sentence: 彼は若いのにしっかりしてるね。
昨日、髪を切りました。
mnemonic: 髟 the long-hair radical spread right across the top of the character. All of it came off yesterday and nobody at work has said a word: かみ.
notes: The hair on your head. 毛 け is hair anywhere else. Three かみ in the deck, told apart by the kanji: 髪 hair, 神 god, 紙 paper.
sentence_meaning: I had my hair cut yesterday.

sentence: あの人は卓球の元選手です。
mnemonic: 元 is where a thing started, the same 元 as 元気. Stick it on the front of a job and it means that's where they started, and stopped: もと.
notes: Same sound as 下 もと, 'under the supervision of'. This one goes in front of a role: 元選手, a former player.
sentence_meaning: That person is a former table tennis player.

mnemonic: 彳 the step radical with a hand and a prize on the right. You go out and you come back holding it. He came back holding rather a lot: える.
sentence: 彼は大金を得ましたよ。
sentence_meaning: He gained a lot of money.
notes: Formal. In speech もらう or 手に入れる do the same job.

sentence: すぐ行きます。
mnemonic: Not in a minute, not after this. You're already reaching for your coat while you're saying it: すぐ.
notes: Also does distance. すぐそこ is 'just over there'.
sentence_meaning: I'll go right away.

notes: 月 reads げつ here, not つき as in 毎月 まいつき. Same 来 as 来年 らいねん.
sentence_meaning: I'll be a college student starting next month.
sentence: 来月から大学生になります。
mnemonic: 来 the crop not yet in, sat on 月 the moon. One more turn of it and you stop being a school pupil for good: らいげつ.

sentence: 昔、ここは海でした。
mnemonic: Strokes stacked up over 日 the sun. Days piled behind you until you can't see past them. Stand here and it was all water once: むかし.
meaning: a long time ago, the old days
sentence_meaning: A long time ago this was an ocean.

notes: 最近 さいきん, 'recently', is this kanji doing the same job with time.
sentence_meaning: The station is near here.
sentence: 駅はここから近いです。
mnemonic: 辶 the road with 斤 an axe on it. Close enough that one swing covers it. The station is round the corner, you'll hear the announcements: ちかい.

sentence: まず相手の動きを見ましょう。
mnemonic: 動く moving, stopped just short of being a verb. Before you do anything at all, watch what the 相手 across from you is doing with their feet: うごき.
notes: The noun from 動く うごく. Uses 相手 あいて, the word for whoever is on the other side.
sentence_meaning: First, watch your opponent's moves.
He kept gazing at that painting the whole time.
notes: One of the 見 family: 見る is looking, 見える is being visible, 見つける is finding, 見つめる is not looking away.
mnemonic: 見 an eye that has landed on something and packed it in tight. He stood in front of that painting and did not move for forty minutes: みつめる.
sentence: 彼はその絵をずっと見つめていたの。

sentence_meaning: I'm happy to have good friends.
notes: A settled, lasting happiness. 嬉しい うれしい is the sharp kind, about one particular thing.
mnemonic: 幸 the shape for a lucky escape. Nothing has happened, nothing has been won. You just have good friends and that turns out to be the whole thing: しあわせ.
sentence: 良い友達がいて私は幸せだ。

notes: The stored thing. 覚える おぼえる is the act of putting it there.
sentence_meaning: I clearly remember what happened at that time.
sentence: 当時のことはしっかり記憶しているよ。
mnemonic: 記 words written down beside 己 yourself, and 憶 a 忄 heart holding the thought. Everything from back then is still filed, and still sharp: きおく.

sentence: 彼女は良い反応を示したわ。
mnemonic: 反 something turned back and 応 a 心 heart under a shelter answering it. You put a thing in front of her and it came straight back, warmly: はんのう.
notes: Same 反 as 返す かえす. Both are about a thing coming back at you.
sentence_meaning: She showed a good reaction.

sentence: 私たちは来月結婚します。
mnemonic: 私 the one you already know, with たち piled on the end to make it more than one. Next month there'll be a certificate saying so: わたしたち.
notes: たち pluralises people generally, 子供たち, 友達. Never used for objects.
sentence_meaning: We will get married next month.
Anyway, let's go to the site.
notes: Sweeps the argument aside and moves on to what you're actually going to do.
mnemonic: Everyone has a theory and nobody has been outside. とにかく. Right, whatever the answer is, we're going down there to look.
sentence: とにかく現場へ行ってみましょう。

notes: 勝手に means 'without asking anyone'. 勝手に決めた, decided it on his own.
sentence_meaning: Don't say self-centered things all the time.
sentence: 勝手なことばかり言わないでくれ。
mnemonic: 勝 winning with 手 a hand, playing every round for yourself and nobody else at the table. Enough of it now: かって.

notes: Does military attacks and verbal ones. 攻撃的 こうげきてき is 'aggressive' about a person.
sentence_meaning: The United States attacked Iraq in 2003.
sentence: 2003年にアメリカはイラクを攻撃した。
mnemonic: 攻 going at something with 攵 the strike radical, and 撃 a hand driving the whole weight down. It covers armies, and it covers what people do to each other in print: こうげき.

notes: The third of the set: 開く あく is it opening on its own, 開く ひらく is spreading something open, 開ける あける is you opening it.
sentence_meaning: Please open the window.
sentence: 窓を開けてください。
mnemonic: 門 the gate again, and this time your hands are on the bar. The window doesn't slide itself. Somebody has to get up: あける.

sentence: 彼はいつも黙って仕事をします。
mnemonic: 黒 black with 犬 a dog underneath it, sat there not making a sound. He gets in, gets on with it, and you hear nothing all day: だまる.
notes: 黙って means 'without saying anything'. It can be admiring or it can be an order.
meaning: to become silent, to shut one's mouth
sentence_meaning: He always works in silence.
Recently, I have been busy at work.
notes: Same 最 as 最初 and 最後. Covers 'recently' and 'these days' both.
mnemonic: 最 the extreme end of something and 近 near. The closest bit of the past to where you're stood. Work has been like this for a few weeks now: さいきん.
sentence: 最近、仕事が忙しいです。

mnemonic: 全 the whole lot and 員 each 口 mouth on the list counted off. Every single person on the team got one, down to the reserves: ぜんいん.
sentence: チーム全員に名札が配られました。
sentence_meaning: The name tags were distributed to every member.
notes: 全部 ぜんぶ is everything; 全員 is everybody. People take 員, things take 部.
Always for bad outcomes. For good ones it's おかげ, thanks to someone.
sentence_meaning: Don't blame others for your failure.
sentence: 自分の失敗を他人のせいにするな。
mnemonic: You dropped it, and within a second it's the floor's doing, or the light, or whoever handed it to you. せい is where the finger lands when it isn't pointing at you.

sentence_meaning: That pond is very deep.
notes: Does depth and profundity both. 深い意味 is a deep meaning.
mnemonic: 氵 water on the left with a hand reaching down into it and not touching anything. Nobody swims in that pond twice: ふかい.
sentence: あの池はとても深い。

mnemonic: 刂 a blade cuts one card out of the deck and drops it face up, a different suit from everything else on the table. I would bet Sue swapped it: べつ.
sentence: 別の本も見せてください。
sentence_meaning: Please show me another book.
notes: 別に べつに is this word plus に, and nearly always sits in a negative sentence. 別 on its own is just separate, or another one.
決める きめる is somebody deciding. 決まる is it coming out decided, often with nobody visible doing it.
sentence_meaning: The travel dates have been set.
meaning: to be decided, to be set
sentence: 旅行の日程が決まりました。
mnemonic: 氵 a channel cut long before you turned up, and the water only goes one way now. The dates are on the calendar already. Ask Kim: a rule is a rule. きまる.

notes: Vague on purpose. Anything from a few minutes to a few years, and しばらくぶり is what you say after a long gap.
meaning: for a while, for the time being
sentence_meaning: He's resting over there for a while.
sentence: そこでしばらく休んでいます。
mnemonic: The landlady drops the bar across the door and sits back down. Nobody is leaving for a good while yet. She barred the lock: しばらく.

sentence_meaning: The Winter Olympics were held in Japan in 1998.
notes: Same 行 as 行く いく. 行く is going somewhere, 行う is putting the event on, and its reading is the odd one to hold on to.
mnemonic: 行 the crossroads from above, closed off today for the race. Someone has to set out every cone, and shin one doing it: oh, cone, ow. おこなう.
sentence: １９９８年に日本で冬のオリンピックが行われました。

notes: 上げる あげる is you raising something. 上がる is it going up by itself: prices, temperature, or you to the next floor.
sentence_meaning: We went up to the second floor.
sentence: 私たちは２階に上がった。
mnemonic: 上 a mark sitting above the line. Leave the dough by the Aga, ruin the cloth over it, and by morning it has climbed the bowl on its own: あがる.

notes: The one immediately beside you. 近く ちかく is loosely nearby.
sentence_meaning: They have a dog next door.
sentence: 隣の家には犬がいます。
mnemonic: 阝 a mound on the left, and somebody else's garden behind it. Whatever they are cooking comes over the bank every evening, tuna rice again: となり.

sentence_meaning: He opened the door.
notes: The panel that swings, and a shade more literary than ドア. It is also the title page of a book.
mnemonic: 戸 a door with 非 stacked up behind it. It swings in harder than anyone expects. Your toe, then the beer, then the whole room going ah: とびら.
sentence: 彼は扉を開けたんだ。

notes: Fingers and toes both. 足の指 あしのゆび is a toe.
sentence_meaning: He has fat fingers.
sentence: 彼は指が太い。
mnemonic: 扌 a hand and 旨 the point of the thing, so this is what you point with. Reach in among the flowers and the sting lands on it first: you, bee. ゆび.

sentence: 試合の結果を早く知りたい。
mnemonic: 糸 a thread pulled into a knot and 果 the fruit a tree finally lets go of. Nobody wants the story of the match, only the number chalked up at the end: けっか.
notes: その結果 is as a result, and 〜した結果 is what came of doing the thing.
sentence_meaning: I want to know the results of the game soon.

mnemonic: 与 is one hand passing a thing across to another. She folds your fingers round it and the hall claps before you have even looked. Ah, ta. Eh? A ruler. あたえる.
sentence: そのニュースは彼に大きなショックを与えた。
sentence_meaning: That news gave him a great shock.
notes: Formal, and it takes the abstract objects: 影響を与える to have an influence, ショックを与える to give someone a shock. あげる is the everyday give.
Also the way of doing a thing, which is the 道 in 柔道 and 書道.
sentence_meaning: I know this road.
sentence: この道を知っています。
mnemonic: 辶 the road radical under 首 a neck, the way running off wherever your head points. He knows this one so well the Michelin map stays in the glovebox: みち.

sentence_meaning: Please take a taxi from the station.
notes: Takes に and not を: バスに乗る. 乗せる のせる is putting somebody else on board.
mnemonic: 乗 is a figure standing up in a tree, on top of the thing rather than beside it. The doors open on a packed carriage and the platform gets on anyway: no room. のる.
sentence: 駅からはタクシーに乗ってください。
特に質問はありません。
mnemonic: 牛 a cow walks in through 寺 the temple gate while the rest of the herd stands in the field. Out of forty of them they took Neil, only Neil: とくに.
notes: Very often with a negative. 特に〜ない is not particularly.
sentence_meaning: I don't have any question in particular.

notes: 形 also reads けい in compounds, as in 形式 けいしき.
sentence_meaning: This cookie is in the shape of a star.
sentence: このクッキーは星の形です。
mnemonic: 彡 three strokes down the right, the marks you draw round a thing to show its outline. He cut a cheese into stars for the party and nobody ate one: かたち.

sentence_meaning: A: Which side do you think will win?B: Hmm... I don't know.
notes: The same さあ gets things moving as well: さあ、行こう. Tone tells you which one you are hearing.
mnemonic: Asked which side will win, he lets the breath out slowly and looks at the ceiling. Nothing follows it. The whole answer is that noise: さあ.
sentence: A「どちらが勝つでしょうか。」B「さあ.....わかりません。」

notes: Same reading as 地 ち, ground. This is the one that comes out of you.
sentence_meaning: You're bleeding.
sentence: 血が出ていますよ。
mnemonic: 皿 a dish, and the mark above it is whatever got poured in. He raises his glass, says cheers, and only then sees what is running down your arm: ち.

sentence_meaning: He kept raising even more questions.
notes: 更 reads こう in compounds, as in 変更 へんこう. さらに piles more on top of what is already there.
mnemonic: The questions got answered, came round again, then a third time on top of those. Sarah, knee going under the desk, stopped writing them down: さらに.
sentence: 彼は更に質問を続けたの。

mnemonic: 用 a thing set out to be used, and 意 a sound sitting on a heart, your mind on it. The table was laid an hour early. Yo, we eat at seven: ようい.
sentence: 食事の用意ができました。
sentence_meaning: The meal is ready.
notes: 用意ができる is to be ready. 準備 じゅんび is the same idea a step more formal.
